title: Minimum Increment to Make Array Unique
statement:
You have an integer array `nums`. A single move chooses any index and adds 1 to the value stored there; values may grow past the input's limits.

Return the smallest number of moves after which no two entries of `nums` are equal. The inputs are chosen so that this number fits in a 32-bit signed integer.
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer
notes:
## Intuition

Moves only raise values, so a value can never move below where it starts. After sorting, give each value the smallest number that is at least itself and larger than everything already placed. Raising any value further than that only costs extra moves and leaves less room for the values after it, so this greedy choice is optimal. A brute-force view counts copies of each value and pushes every surplus copy one step up at a time; sorting does the same bookkeeping per element.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in ascending order.
2. Keep `next`, the smallest value that is still free, and `moves`, the total so far.
3. For each `value`, its final `target` is `Math.max(value, next)`: unchanged if it is already free, otherwise raised to `next`.
4. Add `target - value` to `moves` and set `next = target + 1`.
5. Return `moves`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 2]` is already sorted.

- `value = 1`: `next = 0`, so `target = 1`, no cost; `next = 2`.
- `value = 2`: `target = 2`, no cost; `next = 3`.
- `value = 2`: `next = 3` is larger, so `target = 3`, costing 1 move; `next = 4`.

The answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) extra beyond the in-place sort.

## Pitfalls

- Sort numerically (`(a, b) => a - b`); the default JavaScript sort compares values as strings.
- Values may end above 10^5: `[100000, 100000]` needs one move to reach `100001`, so do not cap `target`.
- Set `next` from `target`, not from `value`: in `[1, 1, 1]` the second `1` becomes `2`, so the third must go to `3`.
- Do not just count duplicates: `[2, 2, 3]` needs 2 moves, because the raised `2` collides with the `3`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `moves` | total increments made so far |
| `next` | smallest value not yet taken by an earlier element |
| `value` | the current element in sorted order |
| `target` | the value this element ends at |

narration.2: Sort so each element only has to avoid the elements already placed before it.
narration.3: No moves have been made yet.
narration.4: next is the smallest value that no earlier element has taken.
narration.6: Place the elements one by one, smallest first.
narration.7: The element keeps its value if that is free, otherwise it is raised to next.
narration.8: Raising it from value to target costs exactly target - value moves.
narration.9: Everything up to target is now taken, so the next free value is target + 1.
narration.11: All values are distinct; return the total number of moves.
